conviction.explanation: At 48x trailing earnings, observed EPS decline despite higher group profit and externally funded capital-intensive expansion create unfavorable current purchase compensation. Backlog and better margins prevent a strong sell; unavailable June cash/debt further limits confidence without being the sole bearish reason.

executive_summary:
Solarvest’s project opportunity is credible: Q1 revenue grew 13.2%, profit 19.8% and margin improved to 12.2%, with RM2.371bn orderbook. Historical FY26 CFO turned positive and simple FCF was RM32.112m before expansion investments.

The entry proposition is weaker than the group-growth headline: basic EPS fell from 2.11 to 1.99sen at 48x trailing earnings, and FY26 equity-related proceeds were RM386.821m. Investment-property and associate/JV outlays exceeded the simple surplus. A modest sell view reflects delivered dilution and premium exposure; March balances cannot establish current June funding.
bull_case: Profitable order conversion could eventually outgrow dilution and turn improving project margins into per-share cash gains.
bear_case: Dilution, capital demands and collections may keep owner returns behind profit growth while the premium contracts.
key_uncertainties: Current June 30 full balance-sheet/cash-flow attachment unavailable; March evidence is older.
Cash after expansion outlays beyond simple PP&E/intangible FCF.
catalysts_upcoming: Comparable Q1 EPS above the prior 2.11sen with maintained margins would challenge the per-share objection.
Current statements showing positive cash after all specified expansion outlays would reduce funding concerns.
